_about: spck.dev UCP conformance coverage — every normative MUST accounted as CHECK (kill-rate-validated), EXEMPT (documented), or GAP. Generated by conformance/coverage/matrix.py --json; the `coverage` CI gate fails if this file is stale or coverage regresses. Each CHECK row also carries its EVIDENCE CLASS (see `evidence_classes`) and `reach` (the independent targets it actually graded on, per coverage/reach_report.json).

evidence_classes.live-wire: kill-tested on the wire against at least one independently-authored server (flower golden / node reference — see `reach` per row)
evidence_classes.fixture-schema: our fixture validated through the OFFICIAL ucp-schema oracle (spec-anchored, not circular)
evidence_classes.fixture-crypto: self-signed crypto primitive self-test (e.g. the AP2 fixture-key checks) — spec-shaped, not independently corroborated
evidence_classes.self-referenced: graded only against our own fixture, with no independent oracle or target — the fixture-circularity class we flag upstream (conformance#79), named here in our own suite

rows.requirement: The A2A business agent MUST return the checkout object inside an A2A Message DataPart keyed `a2a.ucp.checkout`
Create Checkout initiates a new checkout session via POST /checkout-sessions
Get Checkout retrieves current state via GET /checkout-sessions/{id}
Update Checkout updates a session via PUT /checkout-sessions/{id}
Complete Checkout places the order via POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete
Cancel Checkout cancels a session via POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel
Update Checkout performs a full replacement of the checkout resource; the platform is REQUIRED to send the entire checkout resource
Each PUT replaces the entire session, so clients must include all previously set fields they wish to retain
Complete Checkout response is the checkout object with the order field populated (order provides id and permalink_url)
After a checkout session reaches the state completed it is considered immutable
Status field enum is constrained to the six lifecycle values
Checkout response MUST include required top-level fields: ucp, id, line_items, status, currency, totals, links
Checkout status indicates the current phase and required action; the business sets the status
ucp envelope field is omitted on request bodies (ucp_request: omit)
status, totals, messages, links, expires_at, continue_url, and order are response-only (ucp_request: omit) and omitted on requests
Businesses MUST provide continue_url when returning status = requires_escalation (Availability)
continue_url MUST be an absolute HTTPS URL
Platform MUST use continue_url when checkout status is requires_escalation (Platform guideline)
rows.exempt_reason: Platform-side behavior MUST: on canceled the platform starts a new session if needed; the business duty (canceled is terminal/immutable) is checked by the cancel/immutability checks.

rows.exempt_reason: 'Business MUST send a confirmation email after the checkout has been completed' (checkout.md Business responsibilities, L261@01-11 / L265@01-23) is dispatched on a channel the protocol does not define; no checkout response field evidences it, and a conformance run has no principled inbox oracle — non-receipt is indistinguishable from spam-filtering or asynchronous delay. [Scoped: at 2026-04-08 this id is the testable ucp_request:omit rule on checkout id, already covered by schema_check_04_08_lifecycle; the 04-08 twin of the email requirement is CHK-011.]

rows.requirement: Logic handling the checkout sessions MUST be deterministic
Business MUST provide continue_url when returning status = requires_escalation (Business guideline restatement)
Business MUST include at least one message with severity: escalation when returning status = requires_escalation
All REST request and response bodies MUST be valid JSON per RFC 8259
All REST endpoints MUST be served over HTTPS with minimum TLS version 1.3
All requests MUST include the UCP-Agent header containing the platform profile URI (RFC 8941 dictionary syntax)
rows.exempt_reason: 'All requests MUST include the UCP-Agent header containing the platform profile URI' (checkout-rest.md L1211-1213) binds the REQUEST AUTHOR — the platform — per the suite-wide F2 policy (adversarial review 2026-07-03, register note applied): the spec mandates no business-side rejection of header-less requests, so no merchant response can prove or refute the platform's compliance; the tester, being the platform, simply sends the header. [Scoped: at 2026-04-08 this id is an unrelated SHOULD (severity unrecoverable when no resource exists); the 04-08 twin of this header rule is CHK-046.]

rows.requirement: All capability and service names MUST use the format {reverse-domain}.{service}.{capability}
The spec and schema fields are REQUIRED for all capabilities
The origin of capability spec/schema URLs MUST match the namespace authority
Platform MUST validate the spec-origin/namespace binding and SHOULD reject capabilities where the spec origin does not match the namespace authority
rows.exempt_reason: 'Platform MUST validate this binding and SHOULD reject capabilities where the spec origin does not match the namespace authority' (overview.md L82-83) is a platform-internal validation step over discovery data it already holds; a validating and a non-validating platform emit byte-identical traffic toward the business, so nothing the suite can elicit from the party under test reflects it — same subject-binding as the already-exempt NEG-007. [Scoped: at 2026-04-08 this id is 'reject profile URLs not served over HTTPS', testable and covered by merchant_checks_04_08_discovery.]

rows.exempt_reason: 'Vendors MUST use their own reverse-domain namespace for custom capabilities' (overview.md Governance Model, L94-95) turns on OWNERSHIP: whether com.example.* is really 'their own' is a domain-registration/governance fact established by registrars and the UCP governing body's reservation of dev.ucp.*, not by any protocol message — a payload shows the namespace string but never who owns it. [Scoped: at 2026-04-08 this id is 'service endpoint MUST be a valid HTTPS URL', testable and covered by merchant_checks_04_08_discovery.]

Submitting discounts.codes replaces any previously submitted codes (replacement semantics).
Sending an empty codes array clears all discount codes.
Discount codes are matched case-insensitively by the business.
discounts.applied contains all active discounts (code-based and automatic) in the response.
When multiple valid discount codes are submitted, all are applied (accept-both) and appear in discounts.applied.
When a submitted discount code cannot be applied, the business communicates this via the messages[] array.
A rejected discount code still appears in discounts.codes (echoed back) but not in discounts.applied.
Automatic discounts appear in discounts.applied with automatic: true and no code field; they are applied without platform action and cannot be removed by the platform.
A fixed-amount discount code decreases the total correctly and surfaces applied discount details (code and amount).
An applied_discount must include title and amount; amount is a non-negative integer in minor currency units.
applied_discount.method, when present, must be one of 'each' or 'across'.
An allocation must include path and amount; allocation amount is a non-negative integer in minor currency units.
The sum of allocations[].amount must equal the applied_discount.amount.
All discount amounts are positive integers in minor currency units; when presenting totals, discount types are displayed as subtractive.
totals[type=items_discount].amount must equal sum(line_items[].discount).
Buyer consent is communicated as boolean states within the buyer.consent object (analytics, preferences, marketing, sale_of_data) on create_checkout and update_checkout.
Each buyer consent state (analytics, preferences, marketing, sale_of_data), when present, must be a boolean.
Consent is declarative: the protocol communicates consent but does not enforce it, and legal compliance remains the business's responsibility.
rows.exempt_reason: 'Consent is declarative - the protocol communicates consent, it does not enforce it' and 'legal compliance remains the business's responsibility' (buyer-consent.md Security & Privacy Considerations, L131-133) assert a non-enforcement property of the protocol plus a LEGAL allocation of responsibility; whether a business actually meets its consent-law obligations is established by audit/regulation entirely outside any protocol message. [Scoped: at 2026-04-08 this id is the testable allocations-sum invariant, already covered by merchant_checks_04_08.]

rows.requirement: An error message MUST include the fields type, code, content, and severity (all four are required on a Message Error).
The error message type discriminator MUST be the constant string "error".

The error code field MUST be a string; defined values include missing, invalid, out_of_stock, payment_declined, requires_sign_in, requires_3ds, requires_identity_linking, with freeform codes also allowed.
The error severity field MUST be one of exactly three enum values: recoverable, requires_buyer_input, requires_buyer_review.
Errors with requires_* severity contribute to status requires_escalation.
REST implementations MUST use standard HTTP status codes (e.g., 200, 201, 400, 401, 500) for responses including errors.
If negotiation fails, businesses MUST return an error response (status requires_escalation with a type:error message, e.g. version_unsupported, severity requires_buyer_input).
Businesses MUST include at least one message with severity escalation when returning status requires_escalation.
A fulfillment_method MUST include id, type, and line_item_ids
fulfillment_method.type MUST be one of shipping or pickup
A fulfillment_group MUST include id and line_item_ids
A fulfillment_option MUST include id, title, and totals
options[].title is the required primary label that distinguishes the option from its siblings
options[].title MUST distinguish this option from its siblings
rows.exempt_reason: Whether a title lets a human buyer tell one option from its siblings (fulfillment.md Business Responsibilities) is a comprehension judgment: string uniqueness neither proves it (trivially-differing strings do not distinguish) nor is literally required by it.

rows.requirement: options[].title MUST be sufficient for buyer decision if description is absent
rows.exempt_reason: 'Sufficient for buyer decision if description is absent' is a human-adequacy judgment about label content; no mechanical predicate separates sufficient titles from insufficient ones.

rows.requirement: options[].description MUST NOT repeat title or total; provides supplementary context only
rows.exempt_reason: 'Repeat' covers paraphrase, not just string equality: deciding whether a description merely restates title/total versus supplying supplementary context is linguistic judgment beyond any exact-match test.

rows.requirement: options[].total is the required price in minor units and may be null if not yet available
available_methods[].description MUST be a standalone sentence explaining what, when, and where
rows.exempt_reason: Whether a description is 'a standalone sentence explaining what, when, and where' is a natural-language completeness judgment (does it actually explain all three?) that a parser cannot arbitrate.

Identity linking uses OAuth 2.0 for authorization (the 'v1 auth mechanism' framing was dropped; direct OAuth 2.0 against the business domain via Discovery is always available, with the Accelerated IdP Flow as an additional OAuth-based fast path).
Platforms MUST authenticate token-endpoint requests using a method advertised in the business's token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported metadata.
Public clients MUST use token-endpoint auth method 'none' and rely on PKCE with S256 as proof-of-possession of the authorization code.
Public clients MUST NOT embed a client_secret.
Platforms MUST select the strongest token-endpoint auth method offered by the business compatible with the platform's deployment model.
Platforms MUST include user identity tokens in the HTTP Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.
Platforms MUST process WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenges on 401 and 403 responses to user-authenticated operations.
Platforms MUST extract the scope parameter (when present) from the WWW-Authenticate challenge to construct subsequent authorization requests.
Platforms MUST implement the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow as the account linking mechanism.
Platforms MUST use PKCE with code_challenge_method=S256 for all authorization code exchanges.

Platforms MUST validate the iss parameter in the authorization response to prevent Mix-Up Attacks, verifying it matches the AS issuer URI; if it does not match they MUST abort and discard the authorization response.
Platforms MUST call the business's token revocation endpoint when a user initiates an unlink action on the platform side.
Businesses MUST implement OAuth 2.0.
Businesses MUST publish authorization server metadata via RFC 8414 at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
Businesses MUST populate scopes_supported in RFC 8414 metadata so platforms can detect scope mismatches before initiating an authorization flow.
Businesses MUST return the iss parameter in the authorization response.
Businesses MUST enforce PKCE validation at the token endpoint for all authorization code exchanges; requests without a valid code_verifier MUST be rejected.
Businesses MUST enforce exact string matching for the redirect_uri parameter during authorization requests; the token-request redirect_uri MUST be identical to the authorization-request one.
For loopback redirect URIs (127.0.0.1 or [::1]) businesses MUST ignore the port component and match on scheme, host, and path only.
Businesses MUST declare supported client authentication methods in token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported and enforce one of the declared methods at the token endpoint.
When 'none' is advertised, businesses MUST require PKCE with S256 and MUST reject any authorization code redemption lacking a valid code_verifier.
Requests that fail the negotiated authentication method MUST be rejected with invalid_client; requests that fail PKCE MUST be rejected with invalid_grant.
Businesses MUST validate user identity tokens on every user-authenticated request (iss, aud, exp, scopes, and client_id/azp).
Businesses MUST emit a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge on 401 Unauthorized (identity_required) and 403 Forbidden (insufficient_scope) responses to user-authenticated operations.
Businesses MUST implement token revocation; revoking a refresh_token MUST also immediately invalidate all access_tokens issued from it.
Businesses MUST support revocation requests authenticated with the same client credentials used at the token endpoint.
Businesses MUST support standard UCP scopes as defined in the Scopes section.
On RFC 8414 discovery, any non-2xx response other than 404 (network error or timeout) MUST abort and MUST NOT proceed to OIDC fallback.
Platforms MUST NOT silently fall through on any error other than 404 in RFC 8414 discovery.

The issuer value in discovered metadata MUST byte-for-byte match the AS issuer resolved in Discovery Step 1 (which may now be a different origin than the business domain, via protected-resource metadata); platforms MUST NOT normalize before comparison.
Platforms MUST request only the derived scope set (from config.scopes) and not a superset.
On the authorization response, the platform MUST verify state matches the sent value and iss matches the discovered issuer URI; if either fails it MUST discard the response.
The token-request code_verifier MUST correspond to the code_challenge sent in the authorization request; businesses MUST reject token requests where code_verifier is absent or does not verify.
Scope names MUST match the pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.
Platforms MUST treat any scope listed in config.scopes (well-known or custom) as gating its operations behind user authentication.
Platforms MUST ignore unrecognized fields in a per-scope policy object.
On identity_required the business MUST return 401 Unauthorized, a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge, and a UCP error body with code 'identity_required'.
The identity_required WWW-Authenticate header MUST include a realm parameter set to the business's issuer URI from RFC 8414 metadata.
When the request included a token that was invalid/expired/unverifiable, the identity_required header MUST also include error="invalid_token".
continue_url MUST NOT be used to convey a pre-baked OAuth authorization request; the platform constructs its own authorization request.
On insufficient_scope the business MUST return 403 Forbidden, a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge, and a UCP error body with code 'insufficient_scope'.
The insufficient_scope WWW-Authenticate header MUST include realm, error="insufficient_scope", and scope="<space-separated full required scope set>".
The insufficient_scope scope parameter MUST list the full set of scopes required for the operation, not just the missing ones.
Platforms MUST NOT retry an insufficient_scope response by re-initiating a fresh account linking flow; they MUST instead request only the missing scope(s) via incremental authorization.
Plain PKCE (plain) MUST NOT be used; PKCE S256 is REQUIRED for all authorization code flows, and businesses MUST reject exchanges without a valid code_verifier.
Public clients cannot keep a client_secret confidential and MUST use 'none'; businesses MUST NOT require client_secret_basic as the only method when serving native or agent platforms.
Platforms MUST process the structured scope and error parameters to drive authorization flow decisions; error_description MUST NOT be used for control-flow decisions.
The realm parameter MUST match the business's issuer URI so platforms can correlate the challenge with the correct authorization server.

config.providers is no longer a v1-absent placeholder — it is a live feature. When config.providers is absent, empty, or no listed provider mechanism is supported/suitable, platforms run/fall back to direct OAuth 2.0 against the business domain via Discovery.

When config contains fields not defined in this version, platforms MUST ignore those fields; provider entries with an unsupported type MUST be treated as filtered out, and the platform then applies the Identity Providers rules to whatever remains (no longer unconditionally 'proceed via direct OAuth').
authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported and code_challenge_methods_supported:["S256"] MUST both be present in UCP-compliant RFC 8414 metadata.
config.scopes property names MUST conform to the scope_token pattern {capability}:{scope}.
Business identity_linking config object is required and MUST contain a 'scopes' property.

The `issuer` value in RFC 8414 metadata and the `iss` parameter returned in authorization responses MUST be identical byte-for-byte; platforms MUST NOT normalize (e.g. strip trailing slashes) before comparison.

In the OIDC Discovery fallback (Discovery pipeline sub-item 2, reached after the RFC 8414 fetch in sub-item 1 returns 404), if the {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration fetch — where {issuer} is now resolved via the new Step 1 protected-resource-metadata lookup, not necessarily the business domain — returns any non-2xx response, network error, or timeout, the platform MUST abort.

Businesses MUST NOT return stored user-specific state unless the request is user-authenticated and authorized for the operation; they MUST only return values that belong to the authenticated user and are appropriate for the current transaction.
Platforms MUST treat returned business-owned identifiers as opaque and business-scoped, and MUST NOT infer raw credentials from a display value.
Businesses MUST only list providers they explicitly trust in config.providers, and MUST NOT list their own authorization server.

When a business lists external identity providers of type oauth2 in config.providers, the business MUST support the JWT bearer assertion grant type at its token endpoint to accept JWT authorization grants from those IdPs, and MUST include urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer in grant_types_supported in its RFC 8414 metadata.
If no listed provider mechanism is supported or suitable, platforms MUST fall back to direct OAuth on the business domain.
Platforms MUST ignore any oauth2 mechanism entry in config.providers whose auth_url matches the business's own issuer URI.
Platforms MUST treat config.providers entries whose type they do not support as filtered out, rather than rejecting the business's configuration.

For oauth2 providers, platforms MUST discover the authorization server metadata from auth_url using the same two-tier metadata hierarchy as Discovery Step 2 (RFC 8414 primary with section 3.1 path insertion, OIDC fallback on 404 only), treating auth_url as the issuer.
For the chaining path, config.providers is a closed allowlist: a business MUST reject a JWT authorization grant whose iss does not match a listed oauth2 mechanism entry.

Platforms requesting a JWT authorization grant via token exchange MUST include at least one of resource/audience (the business's AS issuer URI); when both are sent to the IdP they MUST carry identical values in the resulting grant's aud claim.
The platform MUST NOT present a raw IdP token directly to a business.

The JWT authorization grant MUST conform to RFC 7523 section 3, with two UCP-specific constraints: aud MUST be a single value (the business's AS issuer URI), not an array, and jti MUST be present (RFC 7523 only says MAY) so businesses can enforce single-use replay protection.

Upon receiving a JWT authorization grant, the business's authorization server MUST validate the assertion per RFC 7523 section 3, with UCP-specific requirements: iss MUST match the auth_url of a listed oauth2 mechanism entry; aud MUST match the business's own AS issuer URI exactly; the JWT signature MUST be verified against the IdP's jwks_uri, and the business MUST fail closed if the JWKS cannot be retrieved.
If no requested scope can be satisfied by an Accelerated-IdP-Flow grant's claims, the business MUST return invalid_scope per RFC 6749 section 5.2.
If user interaction (terms acceptance, onboarding) is required, the business MUST reject the JWT authorization grant with invalid_grant.
When the JWT authorization grant lacks a claim the business requires for account resolution, the business MUST reject with invalid_grant.

Identity providers of type oauth2 listed in config.providers MUST publish authorization server metadata via RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect Discovery, and that metadata MUST include revocation_endpoint, jwks_uri, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange in grant_types_supported.

When processing token exchange requests for JWT authorization grants, the IdP MUST authenticate the platform and verify it is authorized to present the subject token; MUST verify the target business is a known relying party the user has authorized (resource/audience MUST carry identical values when both are sent) and MUST NOT issue grants for businesses the user has not authorized; MUST issue a grant conforming to the JWT Authorization Grant requirements; and MUST return issued_token_type as the jwt token-type URN.

Advertised scopes MUST apply uniformly across identity paths: the same config.scopes map governs availability whether the platform obtained identity via direct OAuth or the Accelerated IdP Flow, and a business honoring min_acr (for example) MUST apply the same threshold regardless of path.
JWT authorization grants MUST be short-lived.

A Business MUST ensure that Constraint Expressions which can apply to the same object (via overlapping paths) are jointly satisfiable; contradictory requirements on the same property are a Business authoring error

When a Business includes ucp.request_constraints in an authoritative response, it MUST emit values conforming to the shared Request Constraints schema, MUST use valid effective paths that select only objects, and MUST enforce every constraint it emits against the next Platform request

A Platform performing preflight MUST skip a value that is malformed, unsupported, whose path selects a non-object, or that it cannot evaluate within its resource limits, and MUST continue with any other chosen values rather than treat the unavailable value as pass or fail

Each authoritative resource response supplies the Request Constraints set for the next request to that resource; the following authoritative response's set replaces the prior set, and omitting request_constraints clears the set
Invalid request_constraints values in a new set MUST NOT fall back to preserving stale values from a prior response, and sets MUST NOT be merged by path across responses
A response containing an authoritative resource MUST supply its Request Constraints set even when it reports an application error; a response without an authoritative resource supplies no set

Request Constraints add no new outcome or error code; passing schema + Request Constraints validation establishes only schema validity, and the containing operation's existing outcome/error contract (including messages) continues to govern submitted-request and runtime outcomes
On a duplicate Idempotency-Key request whose payload does NOT match the original, the business MUST reject with 409 Conflict (REST) / -32000 (MCP) and MUST NOT execute the request
Businesses MUST detect whether a duplicate-key request's payload matches the original by comparing the SHA-256 hash of the raw body bytes (the same digest RFC 9530 mandates as Content-Digest)

Platforms MUST generate a fresh idempotency key whenever they modify the request payload, including retries with modified payment instruments, updated shipping addresses, swapped line items, or any other change to the request body
Signal values MUST NOT be buyer-asserted claims; platforms provide signals from direct observation or independently verifiable third-party attestations
All signal keys MUST use reverse-domain naming to ensure provenance and prevent collisions in the shared namespace

Reverse-domain identifiers (signal keys, eligibility claims, purpose keys, etc.) MUST match the shared reverse_domain_name.json pattern, now extended to allow hyphens, digit-led later segments, and punycode TLDs
Numeric or boolean attribution values MUST be string-encoded as they would be in a URL query string
The presence or absence of the attribution field MUST NOT affect the response or negotiation
Eligibility values MUST use reverse-domain naming and MUST be non-identifying
Businesses MUST ignore unrecognized eligibility values without error
Eligibility and policy enforcement MUST occur at checkout time using binding transaction data (context is non-authoritative)
All accepted eligibility claims MUST be resolved before the transaction can complete
Unrecognized or inapplicable eligibility claims MUST NOT block the checkout
At completion, accepted claims that remain unverified MUST result in type 'error' with code 'eligibility_invalid'
Businesses MUST NOT complete a transaction with unresolved eligibility claims
On eligibility verification failure the Business MUST return an error in messages with code 'eligibility_invalid' and severity 'recoverable'
UCP signs and verifies HTTP messages using RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures across all HTTP-based transports.
All implementations MUST support verifying P-256 (ES256) signatures.
The algorithm is derived from the key's kty/crv fields in the JWK; alg is NOT included in Signature-Input parameters.
Public keys MUST be represented using JSON Web Key (JWK) format as defined in RFC 7517.

Public keys are published in the signer's UCP profile; the publishing contract and the verifier's key-list lookup rule (which key list to read per resolution mechanism) are specified in Profile Structure and Key Discovery (overview/index.md), rather than a single self-contained signing_keys[] statement.
During key rotation, continue accepting signatures from old keys for a grace period of minimum 7 days.
Content-Digest follows RFC 9530 and hashes the raw body bytes; implementations MUST use sha-256.
Proxies, API gateways, and other intermediaries MUST NOT re-serialize JSON bodies, as this would invalidate the signature.
Content-Digest header is required when a request/response has a body.
Signature-Input and Signature headers are required on requests and responses.
REST request signed components MUST include @method, @authority, and @path (all Required).
REST request signed components MUST include content-digest and content-type when the request has a body.
idempotency-key MUST be a signed component for POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH requests.
@query MUST be a signed component if the request has query parameters.
ucp-agent MUST be a signed component if the UCP-Agent header is present.
ECDSA signatures MUST use fixed-width raw r||s encoding per RFC 9421, not ASN.1/DER (64 bytes P-256, 96 bytes P-384).
REST response signed components use @status instead of @method (Required).
REST response signed components MUST include content-digest and content-type if the response has a body.
Idempotency-Key must have minimum 128 bits of entropy (e.g., UUID v4, 22+ char alphanumeric).
Server storage of idempotency keys must be a minimum of 24 hours, recommended 48 hours.
On idempotency storage failure, fail closed (reject request with 503).
On duplicate idempotency key with a matching payload, return the cached response and do not re-execute.
Webhook notifications MUST be signed.
signature_missing maps to HTTP 401 (required signature header/field not present).
signature_invalid maps to HTTP 401 (signature verification failed).
key_not_found maps to HTTP 401 (key ID not found in signer's published key set).
digest_mismatch maps to HTTP 400 (body digest doesn't match Content-Digest header).
algorithm_unsupported maps to HTTP 400 (signature algorithm not supported).

Verification must reconstruct the signature base and skip the candidate signature with signature_invalid if verification fails (ECDSA or EdDSA); under multi-signature handling the request is rejected only when every candidate signature skips.
Verification must skip the candidate signature with key_not_found when the kid does not resolve to a key in the signer's resolved (capability-filtered) key set.
Verification must skip the candidate signature with digest_mismatch when Content-Digest does not match the recomputed sha-256 of the raw body bytes.
The `profile` value in the `UCP-Agent` header MUST be a quoted string containing an HTTPS URL (non-HTTPS URLs must be rejected).
For business profiles, the `UCP-Agent` profile URL MUST point to `/.well-known/ucp`; platform profile URLs are not path-constrained.
A Business declaring the Split Payments capability MUST declare a non-empty `allowed_combinations` array, each combination itself a non-empty array of instrument groups
Real payment handlers publishing non-`card` instrument types under Split Payments MUST publish their own credential schemas
Handlers using foreign-currency-denominated instruments or non-currency instruments (e.g. loyalty points) MUST convert each instrument's contribution to the checkout currency

A submitted instrument set is valid only if there exists an assignment of each submitted instrument to exactly one instrument group such that the instrument's type is in the assigned group's `types` and every group's instrument count falls within its min/max
The Business MUST derive a contribution for each submitted instrument, in array order
For a specified-amount instrument, the Business MUST authorize for the stated `amount`
A zero available balance on an open-amount instrument is a valid $0 contribution, not a failure

If the Business cannot process an instrument with a specified amount, or cannot achieve the final total, it MUST return `payment_failed` in messages[] and MUST void or reverse any authorizations it made
The buyer MUST NOT remain charged for an incomplete split, even though reversal MAY retry transiently

The Business MUST process each split-payments request as a fresh, full submission, without reference to prior requests or responses (split-payments state, including authorizations, does not persist between requests)
When a split is incomplete or has failed, the Business MUST emit a `payment_failed` error for each failed instrument, with `path` pointing at that instrument

If any submitted instrument cannot be processed (invalid credentials, fraud flag, hard decline, expired, insufficient funds), the Business MUST return an error; a zero available balance on an open-amount instrument is not a failure
If the checkout total cannot be reached after applying all submitted instruments, the Business MUST return an error
If the sum of all specified `amount` values exceeds the checkout total, the Business MUST return an error
If the submitted instruments did not match any valid `allowed_combinations`, the Business MUST return an error

On the checkout response, the Business MUST set `amount` on every instrument that was authorized or charged, reflecting the actual contribution, and MUST derive and report the actual contribution for open-amount instruments
The Business MUST omit `amount` on every other instrument (e.g. a provisional authorization that was voided when a later instrument failed, or an instrument never attempted)
The Platform MUST NOT treat prior response `amount` values as preserved state on subsequent requests, and the Business MUST NOT rely on the Platform echoing them; each request is fresh intent

A Business SHOULD accept Complete Checkout, begin the payment attempt, and return `complete_in_progress` with the challenge Action; if it cannot accept completion before the challenge, it MUST return `incomplete` with a recoverable error Message whose `path` selects the challenge occurrence
The Platform performs an ordinary navigation to `config.url` and MUST NOT construct provider requests, parse challenge payloads, or relay 3DS protocol data

The Platform MUST: validate the URL per the Payment Authentication contract; load it in an isolated, visible browser-capable surface; complete the action.ready handshake before presenting the challenge; prevent interaction with the rest of Checkout while outstanding; correlate embedded notifications with the Action occurrence and mounted surface; and close the surface after a terminal outcome
The Platform MUST NOT infer an authentication outcome from frame content, URL changes, or notification diagnostics
When the Platform-facing challenge interaction finishes, the surface MUST send an `action.done` JSON-RPC notification
Platforms MUST ignore unknown params on `action.done`/`action.error` for UCP processing unless the negotiated handler defines them; such params are never authoritative payment outcomes by default
The Business MUST choose an outer-surface expiry that accommodates the handler-defined window (e.g. the EMV 3DS 10-minute ACS challenge-interface timer)

When the outer deadline elapses, the Platform MUST close the surface, treat the interaction as abandoned, and follow the non-successful surface reconciliation path; it MUST NOT remount the same Action type and id
The handler's trust policy MUST authorize the initial and redirect origins before the Platform displays them
A later Checkout response based on server-side provider state remains authoritative regardless of any 3DS surface notification
A Tokenizer MUST verify a binding by exact equality over type and id; it MUST NOT accept a partial match, and MUST NOT reject a request because binding carries members it does not recognize.

A Tokenizer MUST ignore unrecognized binding members when comparing; an extension that defines additional binding members MUST specify whether those members participate in the comparison, and a Tokenizer implementing that extension MUST follow the extension's definition.
A Tokenizer MUST treat binding.id as opaque: it MUST NOT require the value to be resolvable, and MUST NOT reject a request because it cannot confirm that the identified resource exists.
A Tokenizer MUST NOT reject a request solely because it does not recognize binding.type.

Every token is issued to exactly one participant. A Tokenizer MUST record that participant at /tokenize (from identity when present, otherwise the authenticated caller); on /detokenize a Tokenizer MUST resolve the requesting participant the same way, MUST verify it matches the participant recorded at issuance, and MUST verify the authenticated caller is that participant or is authorized to act for it. A Tokenizer MUST NOT return the credential when either check fails.
identity is a participant identifier, not a credential, and a Tokenizer MUST NOT accept it as authentication.
The handler's specification MUST state whether it accepts network_token_credential as a source credential for tokenization, as a checkout credential directly, or both.
binding.id is a required field; the caller MUST send a non-empty string.

When publishing your handler, your specification document MUST include: a unique reverse-DNS handler name, endpoint URLs, authentication requirements, onboarding process, accepted credentials, token lifecycle policy, and security acknowledgements.
Platforms MUST render all top-level totals entries in the order provided
Platforms MUST NOT interpret, filter, reorder, aggregate, or apply their own display logic to totals
Unknown (non-well-known) totals types MUST include display_text
Exactly one totals entry of type subtotal MUST be present
Exactly one totals entry of type total MUST be present
Platforms MUST NOT substitute their own computed totals for the business values
Platforms MUST NOT autonomously complete a checkout with mismatched totals
When display_text is provided, platforms MUST use it
Subtractive well-known types (discount, items_discount) MUST have negative amounts
Additive well-known types (subtotal, fulfillment, tax, fee) MUST have non-negative amounts
Sum of a parent entry lines[] amounts MUST equal the parent entry amount
Each sub-line entry requires both display_text and amount
Each top-level totals entry requires both type and amount
Price requires a non-negative integer amount and an ISO 4217 currency code
